texts.orig: Creating user personas and framing the prompt: It provides her with user segments that you might not even think of, while providing motivations, pain points, etc. To frame a persona prompt, she mentions an example: if you were responsible for creating a fitness band that doesn’t have a screen, you can ask something like “Who would be interested in a fitness band that doesn’t have a screen?” and it provides a list, like people who don’t want to charge it often, among others.

texts.orig: Why all PMs will be AI PMs ▶
texts.text: Why all PMs will be AI PMs ▶

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: All PMs will be AI PMs because she sees all products needing to have personalized experiences and recommender systems, and even to make technological advancements, you need to have an AI-centric view.
texts.text: All PMs will be AI PMs because she sees all products needing to have personalized experiences and recommender systems, and even to make technological advancements, you need to have an AI-centric view.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: PMs should get comfortable with having research scientists on their teams
texts.text: PMs should get comfortable with having research scientists on their teams

texts.label: text
texts.orig: . A lot of PMs are very used to saying, “Okay, I’m going to do XYZ on launch” and don’t know how to approach researchers. Whereas when you’re working with research, it’s more like: we’re going to try this, and then in a year if it doesn’t work out, we’re going to shut the whole thing down.

texts.orig: How to get started using AI ▶
texts.text: How to get started using AI ▶

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Think twice before you use AI for your MVP.
texts.text: Think twice before you use AI for your MVP.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If you need to just get buy-in for an idea that may use AI in the future, just create a Figma prototype and a demo of what the experience is going to be like.
texts.text: If you need to just get buy-in for an idea that may use AI in the future, just create a Figma prototype and a demo of what the experience is going to be like.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Anything where you can get data behind the behavior with users can be improved with AI. For every product you ship, you can always ask yourself if it can be made smarter, e.g. enhancing it with fraud detection; if it’s in health-care you can make it faster or more accurate, etc. Leverage the data that is just sitting around.
texts.text: Anything where you can get data behind the behavior with users can be improved with AI. For every product you ship, you can always ask yourself if it can be made smarter, e.g. enhancing it with fraud detection; if it’s in health-care you can make it faster or more accurate, etc. Leverage the data that is just sitting around.

texts.orig: Don’t fall for the “shiny object trap.”
texts.text: Don’t fall for the “shiny object trap.”

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A model is like a 3-year-old kid’s brain: You will end up training your kid’s brain by repeating the same information again. Saying, “Here’s what the rhino looks like, here’s what an elephant looks like,” etc., repeatedly. And once you’ve done this enough times, then your kid will see the animal and they’ll be able to recognize it. This is how models work as well.
